ranking_revision: Shared y[mask] is multiplied by exp(effect), then both dense A and subset B are recomputed on this single stock-date label table. Dense population target is median of 0.75*N(0,sigma^2)+0.25*N(effect,sigma^2), exponentiated times ten. Sparse target is 10*exp(effect).
predeclared_comparisons: resample log-median SD / independent-history log-median SD
fraction of q20 <= population median, descriptive only
ranking equal-target vs genuinely-better sparse/short candidate
labels: positive y=10*exp(z); population median 10 except deliberately shifted candidate

scenario_z.three_states80: state[floor(t/80)] + 0.3*e_st, three independent standard normal states
scenario_z.fixed_stock_effects: eight fixed equally spaced offsets [-1.5,1.5] + 0.3*e_st; stocks fixed across histories

discreteness: Gaussian inputs; empirical finite sample medians and bootstrap quantiles remain discrete. Exact inverse empirical CDF q20; even weighted medians average two center values. No minimum-direction filters in mechanism tests.
missing_resamples: Empty candidate resamples receive -1e100 before q20, same intent as current scoring; calibration panels always nonempty.
phase20: Each repeat draws phase uniformly 0..19; partition (t+phase)//20, keep both short edge blocks, sample K blocks K times. Expected weight of every date is one, total row count can vary.
moving20: Draw 12 independent non-circular starts uniformly 0..220. Edge dates appear less often than interior dates; this is not a pure phase-only contrast.
scope: synthetic only; no market data; one fixed candidate per calibration history; rank comparisons are fixed pairs, not a parameter search
